definition.def: A project is a task that requires a lot of time and effort.
examples: Money will also go into local development projects in Vietnam.
Besides film and record projects, I have continued to work in the theater.

definition.def: A project is a detailed study of a subject by a pupil or student.
examples: Students complete projects for a personal tutor, working at home at their own pace.

definition.def: If something is projected, it is planned or expected.
examples: This sector is projected to double in size over the next 12 months. [be VERB-ed to-infinitive]
The government had been projecting a 5% consumer price increase for the entire year. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you project someone or something in a particular way, you try to make people see them in that way. If you project a particular feeling or quality, you show it in your behaviour.
examples: Bradley projects a natural warmth and sincerity. [VERB noun]
He just hasn't been able to project himself as the strong leader. [V pron-refl + as]
His first job will be to project Glasgow as a friendly city. [VERB noun + as]
The initial image projected was of a caring, effective president. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If you project feelings or ideas on to other people, you imagine that they have the same ideas or feelings as you.
examples: He projects his own thoughts and ideas onto her. [V n + on/onto/upon]

definition.def: If you project a film or picture onto a screen or wall, you make it appear there.
examples: The team tried projecting the maps with two different projectors onto the same screen. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If something projects, it sticks out above or beyond a surface or edge. [formal]
examples: ...the remains of a war-time defence which projected out from the shore. [VERB preposition/adverb]
